mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 6-month average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 6-month average in the observed window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4%, labor market slack increases, reducing expected wage growth and depressing S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during the low-unemployment period (p < 0.05), or UNRATE remains above 4% throughout the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (household spending index) above its prior 4-month average is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via stronger consumer demand momentum.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward returns occur after the trigger in 70% of instances (IC < 0.05), or the 4-month average is not exceeded.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index below its 12-month trendline signals supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and robust across multiple such contractions (IC > 0.10), or INDPRO recovers above trend within 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for three consecutive months, the persistent low-rate environment supports equity valuation expansion and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average during low-rate periods (p > 0.10), or the rate condition is not met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment months) above the prior 2-month average indicates labor market strengthening and is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during the employment surge (IC > 0.05), or the trigger is not met.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) below their 6-month averages suggest demand softening, predicting negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and significant when both proxies decline (p < 0.05), or the interaction is not present in data.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in CPIAUCSL (CPI) above the 12-month moving average during a recession regime is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as inflation expectations rise.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the trigger (p < 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not exceed the 12-month average in the observed window.
